overview: This period was dominated by Alexei Starovoitov's work on two major verifier improvements: expanding fmod_ret hooks to any function tagged as returning errors, and implementing scalar evolution expression evaluation after conditional jumps. Shakeel Butt also contributed a series of cgroup BPF locking fixes to eliminate races when reading and freeing cgroup BPF state.

patches.title: bpf: Allow fmod_ret on tagged functions and check the return value
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: This patch extends fmod_ret BPF programs to attach to any kernel function tagged by resolve_btfids as returning an error code, rather than only the small set of functions previously supported. The verifier now validates that fmod_ret programs return a value compatible with the tagged function's error range. This dramatically increases the number of kernel entry points available for error injection and observability via BPF. It is part of a 13-patch v2 series that also enhances resolve_btfids with LLVM MC layer analysis to automatically detect which functions can return errors.

patches.title: bpf: Mark the arguments of fmod_ret progs as PTR_UNTRUSTED
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: Companion to the fmod_ret expansion, this patch marks all pointer arguments passed to fmod_ret programs as PTR_UNTRUSTED since fmod_ret can now attach to functions that may receive partially-initialized or invalid pointers. This tightens verifier safety by preventing fmod_ret programs from dereferencing or passing these pointers to kfuncs that require trusted references. The subsequent patch teaches the verifier to use the declared type as a hint for access when the pointer is untrusted, preserving useful type information for introspection without granting unsafe access.

patches.title: resolve_btfids: Describe machine instructions with LLVM's MC layer
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: This patch switches resolve_btfids from ad-hoc instruction decoding to LLVM's Machine Code (MC) layer, enabling reliable disassembly of ELF object files to perform dataflow analysis. Subsequent patches in the series use this foundation to identify which registers reach a function's return value and whether those registers could carry error codes. This is the toolchain half of the broader fmod_ret expansion: resolve_btfids annotates kernel functions with BTF tags that the BPF verifier then uses to authorize fmod_ret attachments.

patches.title: bpf: Evaluate the expression of a linked register
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: Part of a 12-patch series implementing scalar evolution expression evaluation in the BPF verifier, this patch enables the verifier to track and evaluate the value of a register that is linked (through assignments and arithmetic) to another register. By evaluating these linked expressions at branch targets, the verifier can derive tighter bounds on register ranges after comparisons and jumps. This reduces false rejections of valid programs that iterate over data structures using pointer arithmetic, a common pattern in XDP and tc programs.

patches.title: bpf: Add struct scalar
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: Introduces a new 'struct scalar' type in the BPF verifier to encapsulate a scalar register's value range alongside a symbolic scalar evolution expression. This is the foundation for subsequent work on backedge-taken count analysis and cross-register expression linking. The struct scalar allows the verifier to maintain richer information about loop induction variables, ultimately enabling more programs with bounded loops to be accepted without requiring unrolling. This is a v2 revision that incorporates reviewer feedback on the data structure layout.

patches.title: bpf, cgroup: Protect cgroup_bpf state with its own mutex
patches.author: Shakeel Butt
patches.summary: Introduces a dedicated per-cgroup mutex to protect cgroup_bpf state, replacing the coarser global cgroup_mutex that was previously required when reading or freeing BPF program arrays. This allows BPF program queries and cleanup to proceed concurrently across different cgroups without contending on the global lock. The series also adds a check to prevent attaching BPF programs to a cgroup that has already been removed, closing a potential use-after-free race window.

patches.title: bpf, cgroup: Don't lose errors in effective BPF_LSM_CGROUP queries
patches.author: Shakeel Butt
patches.summary: Fixes a bug where BPF_PROG_QUERY on a cgroup with LSM programs could silently drop error codes from the effective program list lookup, returning partial results to userspace without indicating failure. The fix ensures errors propagate correctly through the query path. This is a standalone single-patch fix related to the broader cgroup locking cleanup series from the same author.
